Community Guidelines.

In a canoe, the rhythm is collective. These guidelines gather what the club expects from everyone who paddles with us.

Why they exist

Outrigger canoeing is a team sport: a single stroke out of time throws off the whole boat. The same goes for life on land. These guidelines exist so everyone knows what to expect from the club, and what the club expects back.

The captains lead

The captain leads every outing. Instructions about paddling, seat position and safety, given before and during the outing, apply to everyone — experienced paddlers included.

Respect on and off the waterto be defined

The club's commitment to a safe and welcoming environment, and what counts as unacceptable conduct — the club needs to write this in its own voice before publishing it.

Use of imagesto be defined

Photos and videos of outings and events are part of club life. How image-use consent works, how to ask that a photo of you not be published, and how members may use club images — to be defined.

Care for the equipment and the seato be defined

Responsibility for canoes, paddles and life vests, and the bay-preservation practices the club wants to commit to — to be defined.

Absences, lateness and seatsto be defined

How the club handles lateness and no-shows at training sessions and outings, and what that means for people on the waiting list — to be defined alongside the booking policy.

When someone does not follow the guidelinesto be defined

How the club handles that conversation and what the consequences are — to be defined.

While this document is marked as a draft, it does not constitute rules in force. The safety instructions given by the captains before each outing always apply, regardless of this text.
